newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils mark time as Chicago tumbles - SEPT 11.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils mark time as Chicago tumbles - SEPT 11.

text.p: European vegetable oil traders were playing a waiting game at the close on Wednesday as Chicago futures tumbled following the release of the USDA's latest crop report.
The USDA put the U.S. soybean crop at 2.270 billion bushels, below last months estimate of 2.300 billion, but still the second largest soybean crop on record.

"We have seen this so often, people running around shouting the crop's going to be a disaster. But at the end of the day we finish up with record numbers and that is why people in Europe have been sitting the weather market out," said a trader.
At the close of business European prices had hardly moved from midday.
"It looks as if the weather market is just about over, but game won't be finished until the crop is in the silos, so people will remain cautious for the time being," said another trader.
Dutch soy oil closed 0.50 to 1.25 guilders up after Sep traded at 97.50 and 98 guilders, Nov/Jan at 99 and 99.50 and Feb/Mar at 101.25 guilders a 100 kilos.
Dutch/EU rape oil closed one guilder lower after Sep traded at 98 guilders and Oct at 98.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Palm oil was quiet during the afternoon with prices $2.50 up across the market.
Coconut oil finished $10 to $2.50 higher after Dec/Jan and Jan/Feb fetched $712.50 and Dec/Jan traded at $710 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil closed $10 to $5 up in a neglected market.
